candidates.attacker_control: The boundary token is parsed verbatim from the request Content-Type header (FileUploadBase.getBoundary(), FileUploadBase.java:419-436) by any application using ServletFileUpload/FileUploadBase.parseRequest(). The attacker supplies an arbitrarily long boundary (e.g. several kilobytes) in a multipart/form-data request. No library-side length limit, normalization, or rejection of overlength boundaries exists in this snapshot.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for a length guard elsewhere: FileUploadBase.getBoundary() (419-436) and the MultipartStream(InputStream, byte[], ProgressNotifier) constructor path (358-362 -> 323-344) contain no boundary-size or bufSize-versus-boundaryLength validation; setBoundary() (497-505) enforces only equality of lengths for nested streams, not a maximum. Checked whether size limits bound the loop: FileUploadBase.java:963-981 and util/LimitedInputStream.java only fail on bytes actually read, and the spin loop reads 0 bytes, so sizeMax cannot break it. Checked the EOF path: makeAvailable() throws MalformedStreamException only when read() returns -1, which a zero-length read never does; readByte()'s no-more-data path (414-429) is not reached here. Verified the buffer size on this path is the default DEFAULT_BUFSIZE = 4096 (MultipartStream.java:184, 358-362, and FileUploadBase.java:994). Checked changes.xml (lines 46-51): only the DiskFileItem deserialization action is recorded for the unreleased 1.3.1, so the long-boundary defect is not documented as fixed in this snapshot. Not verified: whether specific container versions reject an over-4092-byte boundary before it reaches the library; no runtime execution was performed.
candidates.impact: Remote unauthenticated denial of service: each crafted request pins a server thread in a CPU-bound infinite loop, enabling resource exhaustion with a modest number of requests; the library never completes or times out the processing of that request.
candidates.prerequisites: A deployed application exposes a multipart upload endpoint using FileUploadBase/ServletFileUpload.parseRequest (or the low-level MultipartStream API with the default 4096-byte buffer); the servlet container must forward a Content-Type boundary longer than about 4092 bytes (within the container header-size limit, e.g. Tomcat default 8 KiB). No authentication is required.
candidates.root_cause: MultipartStream derives keepRegion and pad from the untrusted boundary length (boundaryLength = boundary.length + 4) without validating it against the fixed buffer size (DEFAULT_BUFSIZE = 4096). When boundaryLength > bufSize, ItemInputStream.makeAvailable() sets pad = tail - head = bufSize, so available() returns tail - head - pad = 0 while pos remains -1; the refill loop then repeatedly calls input.read(buffer, bufSize, 0), which returns 0 rather than -1, and tail/head/pad never change. The only exits are finding a separator (impossible, since maxpos = tail - boundaryLength is negative in findSeparator(), MultipartStream.java:697-718) or reading -1 (never returned for a zero-length read).
candidates.title: Unbounded multipart boundary length causes non-terminating zero-length-read loop in MultipartStream (CPU-exhaustion DoS)
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker sends a POST with Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=<very long token>, where boundary.length + 4 > 4096. 2) FileUploadBase.parseRequest() reads the Content-Type header and calls getBoundary() (FileUploadBase.java:988, 419-436), which performs no length check. 3) new MultipartStream(input, boundary, notifier) (FileUploadBase.java:994) stores boundaryLength = boundary.length + 4 and keepRegion = boundary.length + 4 (MultipartStream.java:334-336). 4) skipPreamble()/findNextItem() -> readBodyData() -> newInputStream() -> ItemInputStream.findSeparator(): pos = -1 because maxpos = tail - boundaryLength < 0 (MultipartStream.java:697-718, 817-826), so pad = tail - head. 5) read() sees available() == 0 and calls makeAvailable() (MultipartStream.java:870, 983-1017). 6) Once the buffer is full, tail == bufSize, pad == bufSize, available() == 0 and pos == -1, so input.read(buffer, bufSize, 0) returns 0, tail += 0, findSeparator() returns -1 again, and the loop repeats forever without reading request data. 7) Impact: the request-processing thread spins at full CPU indefinitely; a small number of such requests exhausts the container thread pool/CPU (denial of service). sizeMax/fileSizeMax limits do not help because no bytes are consumed inside the loop.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no container was tested, so the maximum boundary size an upstream servlet container actually forwards, the exact behavior of a given ServletInputStream for a zero-length read (the JDK InputStream contract returns 0), and whether a deployment uses an alternate bufSize are not runtime-confirmed. Test sources and resources are absent from the snapshot, so intent-encoding tests could not be inspected.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption / CWE-835 Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition

arguments.coverage_summary: Reviewed all 63 readable repository files by listing and text search; performed detailed line-level reading of the core request-handling path: MultipartStream.java (all 1030 lines), FileUploadBase.java (boundary extraction 405-436, limit handling 960-999, multipart/mixed handling 1030-1060), DiskFileItem.java (lines 1-689), and build/release metadata (pom.xml, RELEASE-NOTES.txt, src/changes/changes.xml). Remaining files were covered by targeted search for boundary handling, MultipartStream construction, and size-limit enforcement. No test sources, JARs, or resources exist in the snapshot, so behavior could not be cross-checked against tests, and no execution was performed.
limitations: No test sources (src/test), resources, or dependency binaries are present in the 63-file snapshot; upstream tests that might encode intended boundary/buffer-size limits could not be inspected.
No code was executed, compiled, or scanned; the infinite-loop behavior is a source-level inference from the JDK InputStream contract (zero-length read returns 0) and could not be runtime-confirmed.

Whether a real deployment servlet container forwards a boundary longer than 4092 bytes within its header-size limit (e.g. Tomcat default 8 KiB) was not verified against container source or configuration.

Line-oriented reads covered the primary files but not every secondary file (ParameterParser, MimeUtility, DiskFileItemFactory, servlet/portlet adapters) at full depth; those areas remain unaudited rather than proven clean.

Version identification is based on pom.xml (1.4-SNAPSHOT) and RELEASE-NOTES.txt/changes.xml (1.3 released 2013-03-27, 1.3.1 date TBD); the exact upstream revision could not be confirmed, and no CVE or patch metadata was consulted.

rejected_leads.lead: DiskFileItem.readObject() (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/fileupload/disk/DiskFileItem.java:654-671) performs no validation of the deserialized repository field before creating a temp file, while src/changes/changes.xml:46-50 already records a 1.3.1 action to ensure that the repository location, if any, is valid - the documented hardening is absent from the code.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible but materially weaker than the DoS candidate: exploitation requires the application to deserialize attacker-controlled Java objects into a DiskFileItem (no such deserialization sink exists anywhere in this snapshot) and yields a file write into a directory named by the deserialized field. No untrusted-input path to readObject() is present in this repository, so it remains an unconfirmed lead rather than the strongest source-evidenced issue.

rejected_leads.lead: DiskFileItem.finalize() (DiskFileItem.java:561-568) dereferences the transient dfos field without a null check, so an item for which getOutputStream() was never called can throw NullPointerException during garbage collection.
rejected_leads.reason: Robustness/cleanup defect with no demonstrated attacker-controlled path or security impact; rejected as a security candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Header-part handling in MultipartStream.readHeaders() (MultipartStream.java:523-549) plus the TODO at lines 515-516 about limiting maximum header size.
rejected_leads.reason: HEADER_PART_SIZE_MAX = 10240 is enforced at lines 538-542 and throws MalformedStreamException; the TODO is a hardening note, not a defect in this snapshot, and no exploitable condition was traced.

rejected_leads.lead: Base64Decoder, QuotedPrintableDecoder, and MimeUtility decoding of attacker-supplied Content-Disposition/Content-Type parameters.
rejected_leads.reason: Read only at a high level; no concrete overflow, injection, or normalization bypass was identified, and changes.xml lists prior fixes (RFC 4648, RFC 2047) for these classes. Left as unaudited rather than reported.

rejected_leads.lead: MultipartStream.readBoundary() advances head by boundaryLength (MultipartStream.java:442-447) without re-validating buffer bounds.
rejected_leads.reason: head is advanced only after findSeparator() located the boundary within the valid region; no attacker-controlled state was found that makes this index invalid independently of the loop defect already reported, so it is not a separate root cause.

arguments.summary:
Scope: Apache Commons FileUpload 1.4-SNAPSHOT (1.3.1 in progress) - 63 readable files: main Java sources under src/main/java/org/apache/commons/fileupload (+ disk, servlet, portlet, util, util/mime), plus build/POM/site files. No test sources, resources, or binaries are present, so unit tests and dependency jars could not be inspected.

Strongest candidate: a remote, unauthenticated denial-of-service (CPU-exhausting infinite loop) in MultipartStream when the multipart boundary taken from the request Content-Type header is longer than MultipartStream's internal buffer (default 4096 bytes). FileUploadBase.getBoundary() (FileUploadBase.java:419-436) extracts the boundary from the untrusted Content-Type header with no length restriction, and FileUploadBase.java:988-994 constructs new MultipartStream(input, boundary, notifier) with the default buffer and no check that boundary.length + BOUNDARY_PREFIX.length <= bufSize. In MultipartStream.ItemInputStream.makeAvailable() (MultipartStream.java:983-1017) the refill loop cannot progress once the boundary plus prefix exceeds bufSize: keepRegion/pad become bufSize (MultipartStream.java:334-336, 817-826), available() returns 0 while pos stays -1, so the loop repeatedly performs a zero-length read. A zero-length read returns 0 rather than -1 under the JDK InputStream contract, so the loop never terminates and never consumes request bytes - an unbreakable busy loop per request. sizeMax/fileSizeMax (FileUploadBase.java:963-981 via LimitedInputStream) cannot mitigate this because no bytes are read inside the loop. This matches the long-boundary DoS class fixed in 1.3.1; changes.xml (lines 46-51) records only the DiskFileItem deserialization action for the unreleased 1.3.1, consistent with a pre-fix state for this issue. Source evidence for the defect is strong; practical reachability depends on the container forwarding a >4092-byte boundary in Content-Type (Tomcat's default 8 KiB header limit permits it), which could not be tested here. No runtime confirmation was attempted.
